summary: Couch Investor lays out the five names topping his personal buy list for the second half of 2026 — all positions he already owns, arguing the best opportunities are usually already in the portfolio. His framework: he sizes by existing position and uses options to add — selling covered calls against large holdings to collect premium, and selling cash-secured puts at prices where he'd happily buy more. Reddit (RDDT, BUY) is down ~41% from its highs with growth intact (53.5% fiscal-year revenue growth, expanding margins, PEG 0.6); the overhang is AI-related — Google AI Overviews and data-licensing deals with Google, Anthropic and OpenAI — not fundamentals. NBIS (CONDITIONAL_BUY) is a large existing position he would add to on weakness under $200 (he holds a put and would happily buy near $120). SoFi (SOFI, BUY) is down 33% year-to-date but cheap and fast-growing; his bull case hinges on fewer rate hikes than the one-to-two the company guides for, which would make guidance easy to beat, with the 200-day moving average near $20.50 as the next technical level. Meta (META, BUY) he keeps adding under $600 as long as execution holds, despite the capex cycle and social-media addiction trials, with the core ads business improving on AI investment. Alphabet (GOOGL, CONDITIONAL_BUY) he calls a sleep-well-at-night AI survivor with Cloud growing ~82% year-over-year — a happy buyer near $300. Amazon (AMZN, CONDITIONAL_BUY) rounds out the mega-cap comfort names. He explicitly avoids chasing hyped 'bottleneck' trades, preferring to add to proven winners.
